guides.title: Asia and the Pacific: the other shores of the voyages
guides.description: Ports, passages and return journeys linked to the same dated voyages already shown in the Americas and Pacific atlas.
guides.intro: Follow the voyages beyond the edge of one regional map. A departure port, an island stop and a return anchorage are parts of the same journey, with the same evidence and the same limits on what can be reconstructed.
guides.scope: This directory connects the existing voyage catalogue across regional guides. It does not add speculative stages or change the shared movie. Representative mapped anchors introduce the area; the complete dated regional list follows below.

map.scope: Selected documented geographic anchors across the whole regional connection area. Dates label particular visits, not the foundation of the ports. Offshore sightings retain their offshore status.

points.label: Batavia roadstead
points.description: One documented anchor in Bougainville’s Boudeuse · Atlantic, Pacific and homeward voyage. The endpoint is the documented shift out of the road on 16 October, not a claim that both vessels cleared the region that day. Disease affected the crews. The complete connection list below retains other visits and their separate dates.

points.label: Tidore: surviving ships
points.description: One documented anchor in Magellan–Elcano expedition: selected anchors, 1519–1522. Chronological summary, Tidore arrival and Victoria departure. Victoria continued west; Trinidad did not complete this return route. The complete connection list below retains other visits and their separate dates.

points.label: Mactan: Magellan’s death
points.description: One documented anchor in Magellan–Elcano expedition: selected anchors, 1519–1522. Pigafetta account of Mactan, 27 April. Magellan died here. The next leg represents survivors, not his continued travel. The complete connection list below retains other visits and their separate dates.

points.label: Manila Bay, Philippines
points.description: One documented anchor in Malaspina and Bustamante · Descubierta and Atrevida. The corvettes anchored at Manila. The complete connection list below retains other visits and their separate dates.

points.label: Guam, regional landfall
points.description: One documented anchor in Magellan–Elcano expedition: selected anchors, 1519–1522. Pigafetta account, 6 March 1521. Island-scale location; exact landing beach is not asserted. The complete connection list below retains other visits and their separate dates.

points.label: Petropavlovsk, departure
points.description: One documented anchor in Bering and St. Peter: documented outbound anchors, 1741. Smithsonian Contributions to Anthropology 7, p. 108. Departure endpoint; not a claim that the Pacific crossing was a straight line. The complete connection list below retains other visits and their separate dates.

points.label: Pulo Condore, sheltered anchorage
points.description: One documented anchor in Gore and King · return of Cook’s expedition. The crews obtained wood and provisions before sailing on 28 January. The complete connection list below retains other visits and their separate dates.

points.label: Ship Cove / Meretoto
points.description: One documented anchor in Cook and Endeavour: selected outward stops, 1768–1770. Daily entries, 16 January and 7 February 1770. Selected New Zealand anchorage; the earlier circumnavigation and coastal stops are omitted. The complete connection list below retains other visits and their separate dates.

points.label: Bay of Islands
points.description: One documented anchor in HMS Beagle: selected ship itinerary, 1831–1836. Volume II, pp. 563–564 and 610. Regional bay visit; not a claim of remaining at one precise berth. The complete connection list below retains other visits and their separate dates.

points.label: Botany Bay
points.description: One documented anchor in Cook and Endeavour: selected outward stops, 1768–1770. Daily entries, 29 April and 6 May 1770. The landing met armed resistance; the encounter occurred in already inhabited country. The complete connection list below retains other visits and their separate dates.

points.label: Hobart
points.description: One documented anchor in HMS Beagle: selected ship itinerary, 1831–1836. Volume II, pp. 623–624. The complete connection list below retains other visits and their separate dates.

points.label: Keeling / Cocos Islands
points.description: One documented anchor in HMS Beagle: selected ship itinerary, 1831–1836. Volume II, pp. 628–637. Regional island anchorage; shore work and boats are not separate ship positions. The complete connection list below retains other visits and their separate dates.

points.label: Tahiti, Matavai arrival
points.description: One documented anchor in HMS Beagle: selected ship itinerary, 1831–1836. Volume II, pp. 508–510. Arrival observation; later Tahiti anchorages are omitted. FitzRoy changed the calendar from 16 to 17 November during the visit. The complete connection list below retains other visits and their separate dates.

points.label: Kealakekua Bay, Hawaiʻi
points.description: One documented anchor in Cook’s Resolution and Discovery · Hawaiʻi, Pacific coast and Arctic. First Kealakekua Bay anchorage on this visit. The ships departed, then turned back after a damaged mast. The complete connection list below retains other visits and their separate dates.

paragraphs.text: The dated lists retain each itinerary’s original descriptions. A documented landfall, a roadstead stay and a passage offshore are different kinds of evidence. Where the source leaves a gap, a linking animation is an illustration rather than a recovered daily ship track.

The same port can occur more than once in a journey, and several expeditions can share a harbor. Keeping those visits separate makes it possible to follow preparation, outbound movement and return without turning a port into one timeless event.
